Apple's -7% premarket slide (services and China misses, Q4 guidance 9-11% vs 12%+ expected) is the main drag. Two ideas cleared the high-conviction bar today; the rest are watched but not actionable.

ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ideas.thesis: NVDA has a confirmed earnings report on August 26 after close — the single biggest binary event in AI-infrastructure investing each quarter. The AWS +37% and Azure +43% cloud beats this week directly validate ongoing hyperscaler AI capex, which flows through to Nvidia GPU demand. NVDA has drifted ~18% below its May 2026 high of $237.95 despite its AI chips and custom silicon business each surpassing $25B annualized run rates, creating a setup where the stock enters earnings at a relative discount to its own recent range.
ideas.catalyst: NVDA Q2 FY2027 earnings confirmed for Wednesday, August 26, 2026 after market close — coincides with Jackson Hole Economic Symposium week, creating a dual macro+earnings catalyst window
ideas.edge: 61-analyst consensus price target $302.83 vs verified prev close $195.04 — a 55% implied gap per S&P Global consensus. NVDA has beaten EPS estimates in 79 of its last 100 reporting periods. Company guided ~$91B revenue for the quarter; AWS/Azure beats this week are positive read-throughs for data center GPU demand.
ideas.bull_case: Hyperscaler capex commitments (Amazon $220B, Microsoft $175B for 2026) remain uncut and are accelerating, directly supporting Nvidia's Blackwell order book. An earnings beat with upward guidance on August 26 could close a meaningful portion of the $108 gap to consensus target within the swing window.
ideas.bear_case: The 30-yr yield at 5.26% and ~63% market-implied probability of a September rate hike creates a hostile multiple-compression environment for high-P/E names. If Jackson Hole turns hawkish the same week as earnings, even a beat could be sold. China export restrictions remain a structural overhang on addressable market.

ideas.name: Monolithic Power Systems, Inc.
ideas.thesis: MPWR just delivered a decisive post-earnings gap with Q2 revenue beating consensus by 8.6% and EPS by 10.5%, but the more important signal is Q3 guidance of $1.15B at the midpoint — 16.5% above what analysts modeled. Enterprise Data revenue surged 164% YoY, driven by power management solutions for AI server racks. This is a fresh post-earnings momentum setup where the guidance revision cycle has not yet been fully reflected in the analyst target range, and Wells Fargo just raised its price target to $1,800 from $1,700 post-print.
ideas.catalyst: Q3 2026 revenue guidance issued July 30 at $1.14–$1.16B midpoint vs $986.8M consensus — a 16.5% forward guidance beat that will force a broad analyst estimate revision cycle in the days immediately following today's session
ideas.edge: 15-analyst S&P Global consensus target $1,795 vs intraday price ~$1,447 (post-gap) = ~24% implied upside even after the +10% earnings move. Q3 guide at $1.15B midpoint is 16.5% above prior consensus, meaning current targets are likely still stale and further upgrades are probable. MPWR also announced a $500M incremental buyback authorization alongside earnings.
ideas.bull_case: AI server power management is a non-discretionary spend for hyperscalers — every GPU rack needs MPWR's power ICs. With Enterprise Data revenue growing 164% YoY and automotive sockets expanding (1,500+ new in H1), the company is firing on multiple cylinders simultaneously. Analyst target upgrades post-earnings should provide a visible near-term re-rating catalyst.
ideas.bear_case: MPWR trades at an elevated valuation relative to semiconductor peers, and the stock is up ~70% over the past year — valuation already embeds strong execution. Rising rates compress multiples for high-P/E semis. Customer concentration in large cloud providers means any hyperscaler capex pullback (however unlikely near-term) would disproportionately impact forward estimates. Options on MPWR carry wide spreads given its high share price, so defined-risk plays are costly.

ideas.name: Apple Inc.
ideas.thesis: Apple reported its strongest-ever June quarter in absolute terms, but the composition of the beat is problematic: Services ($30.74B) missed by $480M, China ($18.8B) missed by $700M, Q4 revenue guidance came in at 9-11% growth vs 12%+ expected, and gross margin included a ~2% one-time tariff refund that flatters the print. The CEO transition to John Ternus on September 1 adds execution uncertainty in the most important iPhone launch quarter. At $333.43 prev close, the stock had gained ~15% in July and ~23% YTD, making this a classic 'buy the rumor, sell the news' setup. A defined-risk put spread (rather than outright short) is the appropriate vehicle given AAPL's tendency to stabilize after earnings gaps.
ideas.catalyst: Q4 FY2026 setup: revenue guidance 9-11% growth vs 12%+ consensus expectation, CEO Tim Cook's final quarter ending September 1 handoff to John Ternus, and memory chip shortage extending delivery delays on Mac mini and Mac Studio through the iPhone 17 launch quarter
ideas.edge: Stock implied down ~7% at open (~$310) from $333.43 prev close. Q4 guidance midpoint implies ~10% growth vs 12%+ analyst consensus — a ~200 bps miss that has not yet been fully absorbed. Services growth decelerated from 16.3% last quarter to 12.1% this quarter, threatening the premium multiple assigned to the highest-margin segment. Options are liquid; near-dated put spreads allow defined downside risk if the guidance gap takes multiple sessions to digest.
ideas.bull_case: iPhone revenue grew 22% YoY and the installed base of active devices set a new record. Mac revenue beat by nearly 19% above estimates. If the market concludes Services miss is temporary and re-focuses on hardware cycle strength, AAPL could stabilize or recover quickly — especially if broader tech rallies on Amazon's print.
ideas.bear_case: Services deceleration is structurally concerning given it carries the highest margin profile in Apple's business mix. China structural weakness (intense local competition from Huawei) is multi-quarter, not one-off. Memory chip constraints will limit Q4 unit shipments regardless of demand. Leadership transition adds execution risk at the worst possible time — the iPhone 17 launch.
